text: Swin Transformer is a hierarchical vision-transformer backbone (i.e., a feature extractor).
source_span: A **hierarchical vision‑transformer backbone** (i.e., a feature extractor).

text: DETR is a full-stack object-detection framework that uses a transformer encoder-decoder on top of a CNN/ViT backbone.
source_span: A **full‑stack object‑detection framework** that uses a transformer encoder‑decoder on top of a CNN/ViT backbone.

text: Swin Transformer uses shifted-window self-attention to achieve linear-time complexity and produces multi-scale feature maps.
source_span: Shifted‑window self‑attention → linear‑time complexity, multi‑scale feature maps, good for dense prediction tasks (detection, segmentation, etc.).

text: DETR implements end-to-end set-based detection that does not use anchors or NMS and directly predicts a fixed-size set of objects.
source_span: End‑to‑end set‑based detection (no anchors, no NMS) using a transformer that directly predicts a fixed‑size set of objects.

text: Swin Transformer is typically used as a backbone plugged into detectors like Faster-RCNN, Mask-RCNN, YOLO-style heads, or directly with a detection head such as Swin-Transformer-FPN + RetinaNet.
source_span: Typical usage | Plug‑in as the backbone for Faster‑RCNN, Mask‑RCNN, YOLO‑style heads, or directly used with a detection head (e.g., Swin‑Transformer‑FPN + RetinaNet).

text: DETR is a stand-alone detector where the transformer functions as the head (examples include DETR, Deformable DETR, DINO).
source_span: Stand‑alone detector (DETR, Deformable DETR, DINO, etc.) – the transformer is the “head”.

text: Swin Transformer outputs a multi-scale feature pyramid (C2-C5 like ResNet) from an image.
source_span: Image → **multi‑scale feature pyramid** (C2‑C5 like ResNet).

text: DETR maps an image to a set of (class, box) predictions, one per query.
source_span: Image → **set of (class, box) predictions** (one per query).
